$comment: THE GUARD REGISTRY — every enforcement promise this platform makes.
`scripts/guards.test.mjs` reads this file. Three rules make it more than a
1. A `live` guard must name an implementation AND a literal string that
implementation contains. Rename or delete the check and the registry
fails — so a guard cannot quietly stop existing.
2. A `live` guard must actually RUN: an .mjs guard is named by the root
`gate` or `one:gate` script, a .ts guard sits where the test runner
finds it. A check nobody invokes is the same as no check.
3. An `owed` guard names a stage, and ⚠️ a SHIPPED stage may owe
nothing. This is the DEFER mechanism applied to enforcement: flipping a
stage to shipped is what forces every guard it promised to be built,
re-targeted with a reason, or dropped on purpose.
And the tables in PLAN.md §6 and UI.md §10 are GENERATED from this file, so
prose cannot promise a guard that has no entry here — which is the failure
this registry exists for. Documentation claiming enforcement nobody built is
worse than no documentation, because it is expensive to disprove.
